title: Compounding Growth and Forecasting Fundamentals
description: Master the intuition behind compound growth rates, the Rule of 72, trend extrapolation, and cohort-based forecasting.

interactions.prompt: A SaaS startup grows revenue at 15% per quarter. Roughly how long until revenue doubles?
interactions.teachingPreamble: The Rule of 72 says doubling time ≈ 72 / growth rate. It works for any compounding period  -  annual, quarterly, or monthly. For example, at 10% annual growth, revenue doubles in roughly 7.2 years.

interactions.prompt: Spotify reported 180M subscribers in 2022, 220M in 2023, and 260M in mid-2024. What's the most important signal for forecasting 2025?

options.text: Absolute growth is steady at ~40M per year
The percentage growth rate is decelerating each period
Spotify will hit 300M by end of 2025 easily
Growth is accelerating based on recent momentum

interactions.prompt: A D2C brand acquires 10,000 customers/month. Month-1 retention is 40%, and each subsequent month retains 90% of the prior month's cohort. Approximately how many active customers exist after 12 months of operation?
interactions.teachingPreamble: Cohort analysis tracks groups of users acquired at the same time and measures how they behave over time. The key insight: total active users equals the sum of surviving members across all cohorts, not just the latest acquisition number.

interactions.prompt: When a company's revenue grows 20% year-over-year but its growth rate drops by 3 percentage points each year, naive linear extrapolation will ____ future revenue compared to the decelerating trend.

You're estimating a fintech's 2027 revenue. You have two data sources: a 5-year CAGR of 35% from a small base, or analyst consensus showing growth decelerating from 35% to 18% over the next 3 years. Which approach do you anchor on?

options.text: Use the 35% CAGR  -  proven historical track record
Use decelerating analyst estimates  -  growth slows with scale
Average both for a balanced middle-ground estimate
Ignore both and estimate from market size top-down

interactions.prompt: Company A grows at 50% CAGR from $10M revenue. Company B grows at 25% CAGR from $40M. Roughly when does Company A overtake Company B?
interactions.teachingPreamble: When comparing two compounding trajectories, the crossover point depends on both the starting base and the growth rate differential. You can estimate it by solving 10×1.5^t = 40×1.25^t, or approximate by noting the ratio (4x) must be closed by the ~20 percentage point growth gap.

interactions.prompt: Rank these factors from MOST to LEAST important when forecasting a marketplace's GMV three years out: (a) current monthly growth rate, (b) retention curves by cohort, (c) total addressable market ceiling, (d) last quarter's marketing spend.

You projected 260M subscribers for Spotify by 2025 using steady ~40M/year adds. Now a major competitor launches free ad-supported music in 15 emerging markets. How should you adjust your forecast methodology?

options.text: Keep the forecast  -  Spotify's brand moat is strong enough
Model two scenarios: one with retained growth, one with 30-50% slower net adds
Cut the forecast in half to be conservative
Switch entirely to a top-down TAM share model

interactions.priorContext: Earlier you analyzed Spotify's subscriber trajectory at ~40M net adds per year with decelerating percentage growth. Now a major competitive shock has entered the market, requiring you to reassess your extrapolation assumptions.
